metadata.title: SLOPE.jl: Sorted L1 Penalized Estimation
metadata.description: Efficient implementations for Sorted L-One Penalized Estimation (SLOPE): generalized linear models regularized with the sorted L1-norm (Bogdan et al. (2015) ). Supported models include ordinary least-squares regression, binomial regression, multinomial regression, and Poisson regression. Both dense and sparse predictor matrices are supported. In addition, the package features predictor screening rules that enable fast and efficient solutions to high-dimensional problems.

metadata.title: Analysis code: Changing Epidemiology of Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli Infections in South Korea, 2001-2024 - Age-Standardized Bayesian Spatiotemporal Analysis
metadata.description: Reproducible R and Python analysis code for the manuscript "Changing Epidemiology of Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli Infections in South Korea, 2001-2024: Age-Standardized Bayesian Spatiotemporal Analysis" (submitted to JMIR Public Health and Surveillance). Includes age-standardized negative binomial BYM2 spatiotemporal models (R-INLA), emerging hot spot analysis, Morlet wavelet and count-matched null-model seasonality analyses, demographic decomposition, pre- versus post-COVID-19 period analyses, and figure-generation scripts. Also includes the covariate quality-audit and recovery pipeline, a preregistered multiverse over 400 model specifications with decision rules fixed in advance, detection-adjusted reestimation, a health-behavior covariate domain, and sequential-adjustment checks for the handwashing association. metadata.title: QUELL: An On-Device Benchmark of Quantized Edge LLMs versus Classical Machine Learning for IoT Intrusion Detection
metadata.description:
QUELL — reproducibility package.

This repository accompanies the paper "QUELL: An On-Device Benchmark of Quantized Edge LLMs versus Classical Machine Learning for IoT Intrusion Detection." QUELL is a hardware-grounded, multi-axis benchmark that fine-tunes lightweight decoder-only LLMs (GPT-2-medium, Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B) by serializing network-flow records as text, quantizes them to FP16/INT8/4-bit, deploys them on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, and compares them against well-tuned XGBoost and random-forest baselines on three heterogeneous IoT datasets (Edge-IIoTset, CICIoT2023, N-BaIoT). Detectors are evaluated across detection quality, on-device latency/energy/memory, quantization retention, unknown-attack generalization, and adversarial robustness. Under a matched, leakage-controlled protocol the classical detectors match or exceed the quantized LLM on accuracy while costing one to three orders of magnitude less on the same device.

Contents: source code and numbered pipeline (scripts/), experiment configs, the leakage-safe split manifest (results/split_report.json), all raw result files (results/*.json), scripts that regenerate every table (scripts/reproduce_tables.py) and figure (figures/make_fig*.py) from those results, and a figure-value verifier (figures/verify_figures.py). Every number in the paper derives from the committed result files. The benchmark datasets are public and are not redistributed here.

metadata.title: Strain-Augmented CuInP2S6/WSe2 p-Type FeFET: Simulation Code, Benchmarks, and Figure Data
metadata.description: Complete simulation code base, benchmark numbers, and publication figures for the article "Combining Strain and Ferroelectricity in WSe2 Transistors for Fast, Low-Power Nonvolatile Logic and Multilevel Memory: A Multiscale Simulation Study" by Tanvir M. Mahim and M. Mosaddequr Rahman (BRAC University). The archive contains: (1) code/ - a Python multiscale simulation chain for a strain-augmented CuInP2S6/WSe2 p-type ferroelectric field-effect transistor: calibrated two-valley Boltzmann transport of strained monolayer WSe2, a multidomain Preisach plus Landau-Khalatnikov model of CuInP2S6, self-consistent MFMIS electrostatics with interface-trap models (worst-case bound and finite-rate Shockley-Read-Hall kinetics), and compact circuit models of complementary nonvolatile logic; (2) benchmarks/ - results.json with every headline number quoted in the article, including the robustness studies (trap-density sweep, trap kinetics, scale length, gains at demonstrated strain); (3) figures/ - all main-text and supplementary figures in PDF form. Running code/run_all.py regenerates every figure and number bit-for-bit in a few minutes. New in v1.2: finite-rate SRH trap kinetics (trap_mode="dynamic" in fefet.py, detailed-balance emission, study section [8b], figure figS7). Development repository: https://github.com/Tanvir-Mahmud-Mahim/Process-induced-compressive-strain-with-a-van-der-Waals-ferroelectric-gate-in-a-single-device. License: Apache 2.0.

metadata.title: Robots and Minimal, Physics-Informed Features: A Hybrid Framework for Enzyme Catalysis
metadata.description:
This repository contains the code and data supporting the research article "Robots and Minimal, Physics-Informed Features: A Hybrid Framework for Enzyme Catalysis" by Natalia Onishchenko, Eric S. Larsen, Govind Paneru, Kisung Lee, Diana Kolygina, Yankai Jia, Elizabeth Maria Clarissa, Wai-Shing Won, and Bartosz A. Grzybowski.

It includes four ZIP files:

code_for_automation.zip contains the code to integrate a custom-built pipettor with a robotic arm and a plate reader for automated reaction setup and analysis.

experimental_data_analysis.zip contains raw experimental data on reaction yields, summary table with all features calculated for each substrate used to train the models, and the code that was used to process the raw data.

cars_enzyme_activity_prediction-clean-code.zip has code used to run docking, quantum mechanics (QM) calculation, as well as to train and tune the ML model that predicts whether a compound is a substrate for a given enzyme 


Initially published 2025-07-09, updated upon major revision of the paper on 2026-04-23; second revision 2026-07-01.
